clue.text: Score 100 in break to get a game

indicators.note: letters in break are smashed apart and put back together in another order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A snooker player makes a century break during a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and '100' suggest snooker, where a break is a run of pots; here 'in break' tells you to rearrange SCORE plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer, or association football, is a sport played between two teams.

clue.text: Article in gold case is different

indicators.note: the word for gold acts as a case, holding the article inside it

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: An item kept in a gold box stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here; 'case' is the container signal, with the gold acting as the box round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something other is distinct or not the same as the rest.

clue.text: Varying in character, like this puzzle?

explanation.surface: A crossword described as having a varied, uneven history.
explanation.walkthrough: A chequered career has ups and downs; a crossword grid is chequered with black and white squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Of a varied history, chequered means mixed with good and bad; of a grid, it means patterned in squares of alternating colour.

parts.note: a rep is a repertory theatre
air means atmosphere or ambience

explanation.surface: A plea to bring back the old feel of a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to mend it, putting it back into good order.

indicators.note: the words scene and can are to be rewritten, their letters rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Christmas nativity play's scene can be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nativity scene' looks like one phrase, but 'Nativity' alone is the definition and 'scene can' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascence is the fact of being born or coming into being, which is what nativity means.

clue.text: No returns required from this sort of company

definitions.text: No returns required from this sort of company

parts.words: No returns required from this sort of company
parts.note: returns read as profits a firm earns rather than goods sent back or tax forms; a charity-type company needs no profits

explanation.surface: A company that demands no returns, such as tax forms or refunds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' suggests tax returns or goods sent back; the sense is financial return, profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A charity or similar body is set up without seeking profit for owners.

explanation.surface: A vicar who also forecasts the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'). SKY PILOT is old slang for a clergyman, especially a chaplain, as if he steers souls heavenward; read literally it is someone guiding you through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain was nicknamed a sky pilot in slang; read literally, one who pilots through the heavens and its weather.

parts.note: an edge is a border
D stood for the old British penny before decimal coinage in 1971

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a border that Penny used to trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name; it is the pre-1971 British penny, abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment edged with lace is trimmed with it along its border.

parts.note: read as an operation belonging to Julius Caesar, the emperor, who by legend was born by this surgical delivery

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor's military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operations' suggests military campaigns; it is the surgical birth said to be named after Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical delivery of a baby through the abdomen takes its name from Julius Caesar.

parts.note: 3d is old British money written three pence, the coin in the title of Brecht and Weill's opera, not a three-dimensional film

explanation.surface: An opera staged as a three-dimensional film.
explanation.walkthrough: 3-D looks like 3D cinema; in old British money 3d meant three pence (d = penny).
explanation.definitionFit: The Brecht–Weill work about Macheath is titled after a small coin worth three old pence.

annotationWithheld.why: Join a shy Lady Jane (4), answer GREY: 'Lady Jane' gives Lady Jane Grey, but no reading of 'Join a shy' yields GREY; the clue may be misprinted and no source gives the parse

indicators.note: read as fresh or novel, so the letters of I procure take a new, original order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of obtaining an original artwork from a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'original' suggests a genuine artwork; it signals rearranging I PROCURE. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a casino gaming table and deals the cards.

clue.text: Fashionable woman discards a man from Asia

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: the woman's name throws away one of its letters, the a named in the clue

parts.note: Diana is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A trendy woman ditches a fellow from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discards a' takes one A from DIANA, leaving DIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of India is a person from the subcontinent of Asia.

indicators.note: sounds says the creature's name is said like the word for a nuisance

parts.note: a bore is a tiresome nuisance

explanation.surface: A creature that sounds like a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild pig or uncastrated male pig, a beast.

clue.text: Sort of paper that might so describe the Lady of Shalott, say?

definitions.text: Sort of paper that might so describe the Lady of Shalott, say?

parts.words: Sort of paper that might so describe the Lady of Shalott, say?
parts.note: Tennyson's Lady of Shalott lives on an island, so the paper name split as ... plays on her island home

explanation.surface: Asking what writing paper would suit Tennyson's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Lady of Shalott lives alone in a tower on an island; the paper's name is read whimsically as describing her.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, translucent, glossy writing paper used for copies is named after the layers of a bulb vegetable.

clue.text: Pace for the return of the favourite's extremely fast at the start

indicators.note: the first letter of fast is taken, placed at the start of the answer
the return of means the words for favourite's and extremely are read backwards together

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, with the 's kept as S
too means excessively, extremely

explanation.surface: Speed matters as the race favourite comes back fast early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the return of' turns the favourite's and 'extremely' together, giving OOTSTEP; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A footstep is a single step, the length of one stride.

parts.note: semi means half, partly, not quite
the colon is an organ, part of the large intestine

explanation.surface: An organ stop that is not completely pulled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ stop' suggests a pipe-organ knob; 'stop' is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is old term for a punctuation mark, and this mark is one of them.

clue.text: People get taken in by a turn here

definitions.text: People get taken in by a turn here

parts.words: People get taken in by a turn here
parts.note: turn means twisting the handle, which lets visitors in through the opening, not being fooled by a trick

explanation.surface: People are fooled by a performer's act at this venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' suggests being deceived and 'turn' a stage act; read literally, people are let in when this handle is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning the round handle of an entrance opens it so callers can come inside.

clue.text: Arrive at French mountain on foot from this part of Italy

parts.note: a pied is French for on foot
mont is French for mountain

explanation.surface: Hikers reach an Alpine peak by walking in from northern Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrive at' and 'from' are links; both pieces are French words, PIED from 'à pied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Piedmont is a region in north-west Italy, around Turin.

explanation.surface: Asking which battle a Scottish newspaper reported.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scotsman is an Edinburgh newspaper, but here it is a Scottish man: Scots say 'mon' for man, so 'of the man' is MON'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Mons in Belgium saw a famous 1914 battle; and in Scots dialect the possessive of the word for a fellow is spelt this way.

explanation.surface: Being promoted and getting a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise in rank is to move a rung higher; as a noun it also means a rise or boost.

indicators.note: part says only a section of the words Shakespearian chorus is taken

explanation.surface: A chorus part from Shakespeare written for Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' suggests Othello; it is the verb to moor a boat. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To moor a ship is to secure it in place, as with a heavy weight on a chain.

clue.text: Popular success and honour for a jerk

parts.note: a hit is a popular success
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A celebrity gets a hit record and a knighthood despite being a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult; it is a sudden pull. CH (Companion of Honour) is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a sudden tug or pull, like a jolt.

clue.text: Bound to be amused, we hear, by a king

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: we hear says the word for amused is taken as it sounds, not as it is spelt

parts.note: tickled means amused

explanation.surface: A monarch's jokes are certain to entertain, we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' looks like 'certain to'; 'Bound' is the definition, an apprentice bound by articles. 'to be' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee solicitor was formerly tied by contract (articles) to serve an employer.

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for right is taken out of the word

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: A promise of a clear-cut outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outright' splits into 'out' and 'right': take R out of ENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a consequence.

clue.text: Slide, then start to take off

parts.note: to ski is to slide over snow

indicators.note: start points to the opening letter of the word to

explanation.surface: A skier slides down then begins a jump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like a jump; it is a noun, a parody. 'start to' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a comic imitation, a short parody sketch.

clue.text: Handy varnish ingredients, all in one shop

definitions.text: Handy varnish ingredients, all in one shop

parts.words: Handy varnish ingredients, all in one shop
parts.note: handy read as for hands: a finger lacquer, whose name splits as a fastener plus a shine product, both sold at an ironmonger

explanation.surface: A convenient varnish whose ingredients all come from a single store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' seems to mean convenient but means for the hands; the two words of the answer are both things a hardware shop sells.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a lacquer painted on fingernails for colour and gloss.

clue.text: Quarry here is almost sure to succeed

explanation.surface: Where the hunted game ends up, as good as certain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. A hunter's game goes into the game bag; idiomatically, a thing in the bag is as good as won.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot game is placed in the hunter's sack; idiomatically, a result secured in advance is as good as won.

parts.note: pink describes mildly left-wing politics
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A socialist reporter was criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked' suggests criticised; an engine that pinks knocks or pings.
explanation.definitionFit: A car engine pinks when misfiring fuel makes a metallic knocking sound.
